display.purpose: The one headline of a page outside a run: home's next step, the auth heading, Codex. 1.875rem below 640px.

headline.purpose: Dialog titles and the wordmark in the app shell. 1.25rem below 640px. The pull quote in the landing page's cast panel takes the same two sizes at 700 in italics.

card-title.purpose: A cat's or relic's name on its piece, the points tag, token counts, reward-step numerals.

body-sm.purpose: In-game prose: the prompt in the turn block, the rival's last card, result lines, table rows. The event log sets its lines at 13px.

caption.purpose: Rules text on a card, a goal on a round tile, relic text, score sheet lines, italic flavor text.

label.purpose: Sentence-case heading above a group of pieces, the second line of a lane's activate tile, small table button text.

piece-label.purpose: Text on a piece, 11px, ink, bold or black: lane-tile names from 640px, space costs, You and Rival above a score, the Boss tag, the Info button.

piece-label-sm.purpose: The floor, 10px: a lane-tile name on a phone, a die's element name, a key hint, and below 640px the Fires 1st mark and the cat's name in the landing demo.

print.purpose: Jersey 20 at 20px, tabletop only: lane names, Round n, the rival's name, clan names, gauntlet numerals, the log heading, score totals. On the landing page also a rival's name and numeral in the rival fan and the lane's name in the lane showcase's readout.

print-lg.purpose: Jersey 20 at 30px, tabletop only: run screen headings and the two score tokens. On the landing page: a heading on a phone, a boss's name and numeral in the rival fan, the demo's two score tokens.

print-xl.purpose: Jersey 20 at 40px from 640px, landing page only: the ribbon's h1 and each panel's h2, the close included. 30px below 640px.

wordmark.purpose: The wordmark on the landing page's title plaque: 56px, 76px from 640px, 96px from 1024px, weight 800, line-height 0.9, tracking -0.035em, with a 3px ink stroke painted under the fill and a 3px chipboard edge and 2px ink line as a straight-down text shadow. The family is the open system rounded stack; that is carried, not a rule.

shadows.name: panel
shadows.purpose: Ambient lift for white panels and dialogs.

shadows.name: floating-bar
shadows.purpose: The mobile navigation bar (not shown on the run route).

shadows.name: auth-shell
shadows.purpose: The single card on login and signup.

shadows.name: hero-button
shadows.purpose: Soft lime glow under the hero pill button. Defined in the button component; no screen uses it now that the landing demo's confirm is a table button.

shadows.name: rarity-band
shadows.purpose: Strip across the top of a cat card; an inset band, not a shadow.

shadows.name: piece
shadows.value: 0 calc(var(--e) - var(--sink, 0px) + 2px) 0 -2px #b9a47e, 0 calc(var(--e) - var(--sink, 0px) + 2px) 0 0 #17212b, 0 calc(var(--e) - var(--sink, 0px) + var(--lift, 0px) + 7px) 0 -2px var(--cast)
shadows.purpose: Tabletop only. A piece's chipboard edge (--e: 2px token or tile, 3px card), the ink line under it, and an unblurred cast shadow showing 3px at rest.

shadows.name: mat
shadows.purpose: Tabletop only. The sky mat as a 3px board on the cloth.

shadows.name: tray-well
shadows.purpose: Tabletop only. A recess, shaded along its top inner edge.

shadows.name: rail
shadows.purpose: Tabletop only. The docked edge shading the cloth above its ink line. The rail down the side of a match has no shade.

shadows.name: cast-cloth
shadows.purpose: Cast shadow colour for a piece on the cloth.

shadows.name: cast-mat
shadows.purpose: Cast shadow colour for a piece on the mat.

shadows.name: cast-rail
shadows.purpose: Cast shadow colour for a piece on the docked edge or on the match's side rail.

shadows.name: stage
shadows.purpose: Landing page. The cobalt stage frame as a 5px board with a 5px cast in the colour of what it stands on.

shadows.name: board
shadows.purpose: Landing page. The folded cream board and the board in the close, 3px boards like the mat; the cast is cloth cast on the cloth and deep sky in the close.

shadows.name: hero-mat-edge
shadows.purpose: Landing page. The lower edge of the full-bleed sky mat on the cloth, under a 2px ink bottom border.

shadows.name: fold
shadows.purpose: Landing page. The shade on the far side of a seam between two panels of the board, under a 2px ink top border.

shadows.name: wordmark-edge
shadows.purpose: Landing page. The wordmark's letters as die-cut pieces: an ink cut line, a 3px chipboard edge, a 2px ink line under it.

shadows.name: crowd-cast
shadows.value: a bar under the sprite: height 6.25%, inset 18.75% left and right, background var(--cast)
shadows.purpose: Landing page. The flat cast of a standing crowd cat or oversized icon, one sprite pixel deep and ten wide. Not a box shadow.

shadows.name: cast-sky
shadows.purpose: Cast shadow colour for a piece on the landing page's sky bands.

shadows.name: cast-lid
shadows.purpose: Cast shadow colour for a piece on the landing page's ink lid strip and footer.

motion.name: press
motion.value: 140ms ease; translateY(2px) scale(0.99) on :active
motion.purpose: Press feedback on pill buttons, chips, and clickable chrome.

motion.name: auth-enter
motion.value: 320ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); 12px rise and fade
motion.purpose: One-shot entrance of the auth card.

motion.name: skeleton-pulse
motion.value: Tailwind animate-pulse (2s cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.6, 1) infinite)
motion.purpose: Loading placeholders.

motion.name: demo-step
motion.value: 560ms between steps; 0ms under prefers-reduced-motion
motion.purpose: The landing demo lands a turn one step at a time: the firing slot takes slot-fire, its line in the power list fills lime, and the rival's last card takes card-flip and is coral for that step. The landing page makes no sound.

motion.name: table-lift
motion.value: transform 150ms cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.9, 0.3, 1.25); box-shadow 120ms steps(2, end); lifted translateY(-4px), hover translateY(-2px) for fine pointers, pressed translateY(2px)
motion.purpose: Tabletop: a piece lifts when chosen, rises on hover, sinks when pressed. The move eases with a little give; the edge and cast under it change in two steps and are never eased.

motion.name: hand-raise
motion.value: transform 220ms cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.9, 0.3, 1.25); a hand card loses its lean (up to 9deg) and its drop (up to 28px) and rises to stand 12px clear of the bottom edge
motion.purpose: Tabletop: a card in the fanned hand stands upright and whole when hovered, focused or chosen. Its neighbours do not move.

motion.name: hand-lean
motion.value: perspective(40rem) rotateX/rotateY up to 5deg toward the pointer; transform 140ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); mouse only
motion.purpose: Tabletop: a raised hand card leans toward a mouse held over it. Flat on touch and under reduced motion.

motion.name: table-step
motion.value: 380ms for the first power, each next one 12% shorter, floor 180ms; 440ms for the player's own move, 540ms for the rival's card, 760ms for a scored goal, 1000ms for the end of a match
motion.purpose: Tabletop: an answered turn is played back one frame at a time and a chain speeds up as it runs; any click or key skips to the end, finishing every animation and cutting every sound.

motion.name: table-flight
motion.value: 300ms; cubic ease-out along a slight arc (up to 36px), sampled into 11 keyframes; the landing piece squashes 9% and springs back
motion.purpose: Tabletop: a played card or taken dice travel to where they land.

motion.name: piece-land
motion.value: 240ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); from translateY(-7px), 1px past, back
motion.purpose: Tabletop: a token arriving drops into place.

motion.name: slot-fire
motion.value: 380ms ease-out; lime fill, translateY(-4px) scale(1.07) and back; returns to cream over 520ms ease-out
motion.purpose: The landing demo: the cat whose power is firing lights lime and makes one small jump. The match table uses slot-pop for the jump instead.

motion.name: slot-pop
motion.value: sampled spring, about 400ms (stiffness 960, damping 28); translateY(-4px) scale(1.07) rotate(1.6deg), each multiplied by 1 + 0.12 for every power before it, up to 8
motion.purpose: Match table: a cat pops as its power fires, harder the longer the chain, and starts over if it fires twice running. The lime fill is the is-firing class.

motion.name: token-punch
motion.value: sampled spring, about 240ms (stiffness 1750, damping 46); scale to 1.16 and back
motion.purpose: Match table: a food token, a cat or a score that just changed takes a hit. A power that changed nothing shrugs translateX(3px) on the same curve.

motion.name: score-float
motion.value: 720ms; springs out from scale(0.6), rises 34px, fades over the last 30%
motion.purpose: Match table: points scored rise off a cat as a lime chip, and off the rival's total as a coral one. At most 4 a frame.

motion.name: pixel-sparks
motion.value: 420 to 600ms; 4px squares thrown out 24 to 78px and falling 22 to 40px, fading over the last 40%
motion.purpose: Match table: a burst from a cat that scored, a won goal, a won match. At most 12 a frame, 6 under 640px.

motion.name: number-roll
motion.value: 70ms a step, 140ms to 520ms, cubic ease-out; written by a frame timer, not by React
motion.purpose: Tabletop: counts and scores roll to a new value instead of jumping. Set at once under reduced motion.

motion.name: score-heat
motion.value: opacity and scale 260ms; a deep-lime radial gradient behind the player's score, 0 at two powers into a chain and full at eight
motion.purpose: Match table: light that deepens behind the player's total as a chain runs. One of the three lights on the tabletop.

motion.name: table-shake
motion.value: sampled spring, about 400ms (stiffness 4900, damping 28); translate up to 3px by 1.5px, doubled for a lost match
motion.purpose: Match table: the mat and the supply jolt on a big hit, deep in a chain, on a raid or a burn, on a lost goal or match. The table itself never moves.

motion.name: result-tally
motion.value: 320ms, then one line every 190ms; the total punches 160ms after the last line, with a burst on a win
motion.purpose: The result sheet straight after a match counts the player's lines up in turn. Not on a reload, not on coming back to it.

motion.name: card-shimmer
motion.value: 2200ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) infinite; one white band translated across the face
motion.purpose: Tabletop: a legendary in the hand catches the light while it stands up. One of the three lights; removed under reduced motion.

motion.name: cloth-light
motion.value: 26s ease-in-out infinite alternate; a faint white radial patch the size of the screen, translated 16% by 9%
motion.purpose: The run route: a slow light drifting on the cloth, under every piece. One of the three lights; still under reduced motion; absent from the landing page.

motion.name: card-flip
motion.value: 380ms cubic-bezier(0.45, 0, 0.3, 1); scaleX 1 to 0.04 to 1.04 to 1
motion.purpose: Tabletop, the landing demo included: the rival's card turns over and comes back coral.

motion.name: die-roll
motion.value: 340ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), each die 30ms after the last; from translateY(-9px) rotate(-120deg), a small bounce
motion.purpose: Tabletop: rerolled dice tumble in one after another.

motion.name: rival-hold
motion.purpose: Tabletop: the rival's last card stays coral after it turns, with or without motion.

motion.name: climb-step
motion.value: as played, each written length times the pace: 300ms opening pose; 500ms camera push or a window shutting; 750ms up the wall; 300ms landing; 275ms a floor of the tilt; 525ms a rival rising (450ms more on a boss's dark window); 600ms the roof pennant; 1125ms the pull back; 500ms the title card
motion.purpose: Tabletop: the climb between matches is played one frame at a time, like a turn.

motion.name: climb-pace
motion.value: 1.25: CLIMB_PACE in src/components/run/climb.ts, read by the stylesheet as --pace; every climb duration is calc(<written ms> * var(--pace)); the rests are not scaled
motion.purpose: Tabletop: the one number that sets how slowly the climb plays.

motion.name: climb-hop
motion.value: as played: transform 700ms steps(8, end) between ledges with a one-pixel scrabble left and right (175ms steps(1, end), four times), then the crowd's hop (450ms steps(1, end)) and two white dust pixels (350ms steps(3, end)) on landing; walking in at the foot is 20 pixels in 450ms steps(5, end)
motion.purpose: Tabletop: Hadu goes up one floor of the tower.

motion.name: climb-window
motion.value: transform 300ms steps(3, end) as played; translateY 100% dark, 37.5% looking over the sill, 0 out
motion.purpose: Tabletop: a rival slides up into its window.

motion.name: climb-camera
motion.value: one transform on the tower inside a clipped stage fixed over the whole window (inset 0, 100dvh): translate so the framed point sits at 50cqw and 44cqh, never further left than the window's edge, scale 1 (far back) or 2 (close); each beat's own duration, cubic-bezier(0.45, 0, 0.2, 1); rounded to a whole pixel. One tower pixel is 2px, and 3px from 636 tall by 468 wide, 4px from 848 by 624, 5px from 1060 by 780, 6px from 1272 by 936
motion.purpose: Tabletop: the climb is shot like a scene. The camera pushes in on Hadu, follows him up the wall, crosses to the window, and pulls back at the roof.

motion.name: climb-bars
motion.value: two ink bars, 11cqh each, translateY from off the window's edge, 400ms as played, cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); outside the box that shakes
motion.purpose: Tabletop: in whenever the climb's camera is close, out when it is far back.

motion.name: title-slam
motion.value: 425ms as played, cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); from translateY(-36px) scale(1.12), past by 3px, settles; no fade
motion.purpose: Tabletop: the climb's title card (coral for a rival, lime at the roof) comes down over the lower bar on the last two beats.

motion.name: climb-rest
motion.value: 1400ms; 2200ms under reduced motion, where only the last frame is shown
motion.purpose: Tabletop: the last frame of a climb rests, then gives way to the next screen. Any click or key leaves at once.

motion.name: crowd-bob
motion.value: 1600ms steps(1, end) infinite; translateY(0) then translateY(-2px); animation-delay calc(var(--i) * -290ms)
motion.purpose: Landing page: each crowd cat and oversized icon idles on a 2px two-step bob, staggered so no two move together.

motion.name: crowd-hop
motion.value: 360ms steps(1, end), once; translateY 0, -10px, -14px, -6px, 0; animation-delay calc(var(--i) * 50ms); three times when the round is won
motion.purpose: Landing page: the crowd hops with the firing chain. The cluster right of the stage hops on the first slot to fire, the plaque's cat on the middle one, the left cluster on the last; every crowd cat hops three times when the round is won.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: all animation and transition durations 0.01ms; the tabletop lands the whole turn at once with one settle sound, sets numbers at once, and skips flights, pops, floats, sparks, shakes, the hand lean, the shimmer, the cloth light and the result tally; the landing crowd's animations are removed and the demo's steps land with no delay
motion.purpose: Applied under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

sound.name: source
sound.value: Web Audio API oscillators and filtered noise from recipes in src/components/run/sfx/recipes.ts; no audio files, no library
sound.purpose: Every sound effect in a run.

sound.name: chain-ladder
sound.value: major pentatonic from E4 (329.63Hz), one step a power, capped at step 12
sound.purpose: The pitch of a power climbs with the chain; a power that changed nothing plays a dull 185Hz note and does not climb.

sound.name: press
sound.value: every press on a run's screens makes one sound: its handler's own, else the falling click (sine 760Hz to 560Hz) from a window listener in src/components/run/sfx/ClickSound.tsx; a cobalt table button and a move sent play confirm (triangle G5 then C6)
sound.purpose: Nothing pressed in a run is silent, and nothing is heard twice.

sound.name: cat-voices
sound.value: src/components/run/sfx/voices.ts: 26 pitches a semitone apart from A3 (220Hz), one a cat; contour by archetype, timbre by element (triangle, sine, square at 0.1 at most; no sawtooth, no noise); longer and ornamented by rarity; 0.45s at most
sound.purpose: A cat is heard in its own voice when it is chosen or turned over to read.

sound.name: limits
sound.value: peak note gain 0.5; master gain 0.8 full, 0.28 quiet, 0 muted; one limiter; 14 voices at most; longest voice 1.6s
sound.purpose: A long chain cannot clip or pile up.

sound.name: music
sound.value: tracks in src/components/run/music/tracks.ts: bpm, root, scale and bars of four 16-step parts (lead, arp, bass, drums) written as scale degrees; scheduled a bar at a time 200ms ahead of the bar line; 400ms crossfade on a change of tune
sound.purpose: One tune per screen of a run (clan pick, tower, roof, reward, run won, run lost) and one theme per rival; the opening hand plays the rival's theme without its lead and drums.

sound.name: music-limits
sound.value: peak note gain 0.14; music bus 0.8 under the master; not counted against the 14 voices and not cut by a skip
sound.purpose: An effect always sits on top of the tune, and a skip never chops it.

sound.name: control
sound.value: localStorage key hadumon:sound: full, quiet or muted; default full. localStorage key hadumon:music: on or off; default on
sound.purpose: The speaker corner button cycles the three and is the master of effects and music alike; the note button beside it turns the music alone off. Nothing plays in a hidden tab; a skip cuts every effect voice and plays one settle sound.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Cobalt capsule for the one action that moves the page forward. Chrome only: dialogs, home, codex, auth, landing. Not used on the tabletop.
components.css: .ds-btn{font-family:var(--font-display, ui-rounded, 'Avenir Next', 'Trebuchet MS', system-ui, sans-serif);display:inline-flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;gap:8px;min-height:48px;padding:12px 20px;border:1px solid transparent;border-radius:999px;font-size:14px;font-weight:600;letter-spacing:-0.025em;cursor:pointer;transition:transform 140ms ease,box-shadow 140ms ease,filter 140ms ease}.ds-btn:active{transform:translateY(2px) scale(.99)}.ds-btn:focus-visible{outline:3px solid var(--color-cobalt,#1557d8);outline-offset:3px}.ds-btn:disabled{opacity:.45;cursor:not-allowed}.ds-btn-primary{background:var(--color-cobalt,#1557d8);border-color:var(--color-cobalt,#1557d8);color:#fff}.ds-btn-primary:hover{background:var(--color-cobalt-dark,#0d3c9d)}

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Soft sky capsule for cancel, back, and retry.
components.css: .ds-btn{font-family:var(--font-display, ui-rounded, 'Avenir Next', 'Trebuchet MS', system-ui, sans-serif);display:inline-flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;gap:8px;min-height:48px;padding:12px 20px;border:1px solid transparent;border-radius:999px;font-size:14px;font-weight:600;letter-spacing:-0.025em;cursor:pointer;transition:transform 140ms ease,box-shadow 140ms ease,filter 140ms ease}.ds-btn:active{transform:translateY(2px) scale(.99)}.ds-btn:focus-visible{outline:3px solid var(--color-cobalt,#1557d8);outline-offset:3px}.ds-btn:disabled{opacity:.45;cursor:not-allowed}.ds-btn-secondary{background:var(--color-sky-soft,#e7f7fd);color:var(--color-ink,#17212b)}.ds-btn-secondary:hover{background:var(--color-sky-surface,#a9ddf5)}

components.name: Filter Chips
components.description: Single-choice filter pills in the codex; the selected chip is cobalt.
components.css: .ds-pip{display:inline-block;width:12px;height:12px;border:2px solid var(--color-ink,#17212b);flex-shrink:0}.ds-chips{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:6px}.ds-chip{font-family:var(--font-display, ui-rounded, 'Avenir Next', 'Trebuchet MS', system-ui, sans-serif);display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:6px;min-height:44px;padding:0 12px;border-radius:999px;border:1px solid rgb(23 33 43 / .15);background:#fff;color:var(--color-ink,#17212b);font-size:14px;font-weight:700;cursor:pointer;transition:transform 140ms ease}.ds-chip:hover{background:var(--color-sky-soft,#e7f7fd)}.ds-chip[aria-pressed=true]{background:var(--color-cobalt,#1557d8);border-color:var(--color-cobalt,#1557d8);color:#fff}.ds-chip:active{transform:translateY(2px) scale(.99)}.ds-chip:focus-visible{outline:3px solid var(--color-cobalt,#1557d8);outline-offset:3px}

components.name: Text Field
components.description: White field with an edge border; the border turns cobalt on focus.

components.name: Panel
components.description: The standard chrome container: white, rounded, hairline, one soft shadow.
components.html:
Recent runs

Nothing on record. Finish a run, win or lose, and it is written down here.
components.css: .ds-panel{font-family:var(--font-display, ui-rounded, 'Avenir Next', 'Trebuchet MS', system-ui, sans-serif);max-width:420px;padding:16px;background:#fff;border:1px solid rgb(23 33 43 / .08);border-radius:20px;box-shadow:0 10px 30px rgb(23 33 43 / .08);color:var(--color-ink,#17212b)}.ds-panel h2{margin:0 0 12px;font-size:18px;font-weight:800;letter-spacing:-0.025em;line-height:1.05}.ds-panel p{margin:0;font-size:16px;line-height:1.45;color:var(--color-ink-soft,#5b6c7d)}

components.name: Navigation Rail
components.description: Desktop rail: wordmark and three destinations; the active one is cobalt.
components.html: HaduMonHomePlayCodex

components.name: Cat Card
components.description: The signature piece: sprite, name, cost pips, lime points tag, and the power in words. Shown flat, as it is outside the tabletop; on the tabletop it gains a 3px chipboard edge. Common rarity band shown.
components.html:
Flameclaw

2

When activated: gain 1 Flame essence.
components.css: .ds-pip{display:inline-block;width:12px;height:12px;border:2px solid var(--color-ink,#17212b);flex-shrink:0}.ds-cat-card{font-family:var(--font-display, ui-rounded, 'Avenir Next', 'Trebuchet MS', system-ui, sans-serif);display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:8px;width:208px;padding:8px;background:var(--color-cream,#fff8e7);color:var(--color-ink,#17212b);border:2px solid var(--color-ink,#17212b);box-shadow:inset 0 3px 0 #9aa9b7}.ds-cat-head{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:8px}.ds-cat-id{min-width:0;flex:1}.ds-cat-name{margin:0;font-size:14px;font-weight:800;letter-spacing:-0.025em;line-height:1.25}.ds-cat-cost{display:flex;gap:4px;margin-top:4px}.ds-cat-points{margin:0;padding:0 6px;font-size:14px;font-weight:800;line-height:24px;background:var(--color-lime,#d8ff4f);border:2px solid var(--color-ink,#17212b)}.ds-cat-rule{margin:0;padding-top:6px;border-top:1px solid rgb(23 33 43 / .2);font-size:12px;line-height:1.375}

components.name: Feeder Dice
components.description: Square dice holding an essence pip; a chosen die fills lime (and lifts 4px on the tabletop). Shown flat, as in the landing demo.
components.css: .ds-dice{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(5,minmax(0,1fr));gap:6px;max-width:384px;margin:0;padding:0;list-style:none}.ds-die{font-family:var(--font-display, ui-rounded, 'Avenir Next', 'Trebuchet MS', system-ui, sans-serif);display:flex;flex-direction:column;align-items:center;justify-content:center;gap:4px;width:100%;min-height:48px;padding:6px 4px;background:#fff;color:var(--color-ink,#17212b);border:2px solid var(--color-ink,#17212b);font-size:10px;font-weight:700;line-height:1;cursor:pointer}.ds-die-pip{width:22px;height:22px;box-sizing:border-box;border:2px solid var(--color-ink,#17212b)}.ds-die:hover{background:var(--color-sky-soft,#e7f7fd)}.ds-die[aria-pressed=true],.ds-die[aria-pressed=true]:hover{background:var(--color-lime,#d8ff4f)}.ds-die:focus-visible{outline:3px solid var(--color-cobalt,#1557d8);outline-offset:3px}

components.name: Table Button
components.description: An action on the tabletop as a piece: cobalt for the one confirm, cream for the rest. Square, 2px ink, a 2px edge that sinks when pressed. Three sizes (40, 48, 56px); the large one is the landing page's "Start a run", a link in the primary variant.

narrative.overview:
HaduMon is a board game laid out on a warm cream table. Two materials share the screen and never blend. The page chrome (navigation, panels, dialogs, pill buttons, the account form) is soft: white surfaces, rounded corners, faint borders, one diffuse shadow. The game pieces (cat cards, lanes and spaces, dice, essence pips, score tags) are hard: square corners, a 2px near-black border, flat fills. A player can tell at a glance what is furniture and what is in play.

The pieces come in two states of the same material, and the scope decides which. On home, the codex, login, signup, and in every dialog a piece is flat: border and fill, no thickness. Inside the tabletop the same pieces are die-cut cardboard: each one has a chipboard edge straight down and an unblurred cast shadow, and it lies on a woven cream cloth. Two surfaces are tabletops: the run route (`/run`: clan pick, the opening hand, the match, the match result, reward pick, the climb between matches, the run summary) and the landing page. The scope is one class, `.tabletop`. On the run route it is opened by `TableSurface`; the landing page opens it on its own root, because `TableSurface` also carries the signed-in ways off a run's table. A piece carries the `piece` class everywhere and only gains its thickness inside the scope.

The match is a table you sit at, not a dashboard you read, and nothing of the app stands around it: a white rail down the left holds the rival and the rounds and, under an ink line, the player's turn (scores, food, prompt, confirm); the shared supply and the player's sky mat with three printed lanes lie on the cloth in the centre; a score sheet, the relics and the log stand in a slim column to the right; and the hand is held as a fan along the bottom edge. There are no white rounded panels on the table. Counts are tokens, piles, and cubes; what the board says about itself is printed on it in a pixel face.

The cats are 16x16 pixel sprites: chibi, front-facing, a near-black outline, three fur tones taken from the cat's element, and eyes tinted by rarity. Hadu alone wears his own colours, a black-and-white tuxedo with a pink nose. They are drawn as inline SVG and scaled in whole pixels. The tabletop adds a small set of 8x8 pixel icons drawn the same way (yarn, die, paw, den, card, cached, tucked, goal, chevron). The six rivals are sprites too, all in the rival coral, met at the windows of the grey pixel tower a run climbs between matches. Sprites, these icons and the tower are the only imagery. There are no photographs, no raster creature art, no gradients, and no emoji.

Density follows the game. The table is compact (10px between zones, 6px between pieces) because every rule the player needs has to be on the card or the board. Home, codex, and auth breathe more (16 to 36px). Copy is dry and factual, in sentence case.

The public landing page (`src/components/landing/LandingPage.tsx`, shown at `/` to a signed-out visitor) is the one Persuade surface. It is the tabletop at page scale, laid out as the front of the game's box, with no app shell and no white panel. From the top: an ink lid strip with the two account buttons; a full-bleed sky mat printed with paws and yarn; on it a cream title plaque with the wordmark and Hadu perched on top, a lime ribbon carrying the h1, and a thick cobalt stage frame holding one playable Hunt round run by the real match engine; a crowd of cats standing around the frame; then one cream board on the cloth, folded into four panels (the lead, the cats, the rows, the rivals); a sky closing band; and an ink footer. It is built from the table's own pieces (cat cards, dice, food tokens, the mat, tray wells, nameplates, turn cubes, score tokens, table buttons) and adds only what the match table has no use for: the lid strip, the plaque and ribbon, the stage frame, the folded board, and the crowd.
keyCharacteristics: Warm cream canvas; sky blue for the board and the home hero.
Two materials: rounded white chrome, square 2px-ink game pieces.
Pieces are flat on home, the codex, auth, and in dialogs, and die-cut cardboard with a straight-down edge inside the tabletop (the run route and the landing page).
Cobalt is the action, lime is the player's, coral is the rival's.
16x16 pixel cats and 8x8 pixel icons as inline SVG, the only imagery.
One rounded bold type voice, plus a pixel print face on the tabletop at 20px and 30px, and at 40px for a heading on the landing page.
The landing page is the front of the box: lid strip, sky mat, title plaque, lime ribbon, cobalt stage frame, a crowd of cats, one folded cream board.
Every state has a border, fill, or height change, never colour alone on text.

rules.name: The Lime Is Yours Rule
rules.body: Lime marks something the player chose, holds, or won. It is never decoration and never the rival's. One exception is named: the ribbon under the landing wordmark, which carries the page's h1, is lime although it is nothing the player chose, holds, or won. No other surface takes it.

rules.name: The Coral Is Theirs Rule
rules.body: Coral marks the rival and what the rival does; outside the table it also marks a destructive act. It never marks a decision the player owes, and never a piece the player owns. Text sitting on a coral fill is ink.

rules.name: The Waiting Piece Rule
rules.body: A piece of the player's that is waiting on an answer takes a cobalt frame with a lime inner line. A card marked for trimming takes the cobalt chosen frame and an ink tag. Neither takes coral.

rules.name: The Ink On Colour Rule
rules.body: Text on lime, coral, sky, cream, or an element hue is ink. White text appears only on cobalt. The inverses are the small ink tag and, on the landing page, the lid strip and the footer, which carry cream text.

rules.name: The Element Stays On The Cat Rule
rules.body: Element hues colour sprites, pips, and dice. Panels, buttons, and headings never take an element colour.

rules.name: The Two Sizes Of Print Rule
rules.body: The pixel face is drawn on a 20px grid, so on the match table it is set at 20px and 30px and nowhere between. The landing page adds one step, for a heading only: 30px on a phone and 40px from 640px, on the ribbon's h1 and each panel's h2. Print is for what is printed on the board (names, numerals, totals, headings on the table), never for rules text, and never outside the tabletop.

rules.name: The Numbers Line Up Rule
rules.body: Every score, count, and cost that can change uses tabular figures.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Headings, buttons, and labels are sentence case. Uppercase is reserved for two small marks: the filter group label and the Boss tag in the codex.

rules.name: The Rules Are On The Piece Rule
rules.body: A card states its own cost, points, and power in words. Type on a piece may get small, but it stays ink and stays bold enough to read on a phone: 11px on a piece, 10px only for a lane-tile name on a phone, a die's name, and a key hint.

rules.name: The Scoped Thickness Rule
rules.body: A game piece casts no shadow outside the tabletop: on home, the codex, auth, and in every dialog it is border and fill. Inside the tabletop (the run route and the landing page) every piece has an edge and a cast shadow, straight down and unblurred. No piece anywhere takes a blurred shadow or a sideways offset.

rules.name: The Frame Means State Rule
rules.body: On the tabletop a piece's state is its border: cobalt border for open to pick, cobalt border with a 2px cobalt inner line for chosen, cobalt border with a 2px cobalt and a 2px lime inner line for waiting on the player. A chosen piece is also lifted. No ring is drawn outside a piece's border.

rules.name: The Three Heights Rule
rules.body: A thing on the table is print (0), a token or tile (2px), or a card (3px). Only a stack is taller, and its height is its count. The landing page's title plaque and stage frame are the box's furniture, not things in play, and stand 5px.

dos: Do decide which material a new element is before styling it. In play: square, 2px ink border, flat fill. Around play: rounded, white, hairline, soft shadow.

Do decide which scope a piece is in. Inside the tabletop (`TableSurface` on the run route, the landing page's own root) it is cardboard: give it the `piece` class and let the tabletop add the edge. Anywhere else it stays flat.
Do pick one of the three heights for a new thing on the table: print, token or tile (2px), card (3px).

Do render every cat through `src/components/PixelSprite.tsx` at a whole-pixel multiple of 16 where the layout allows, and every mark on a piece through `src/components/PixelIcon.tsx` at a multiple of 8.
Do use ink text on lime, coral, sky, and cream; white text only on cobalt.
Do show state on the table with the frame (cobalt border, cobalt inner line, lime inner line) and with height (lifted 4px, pressed 2px), and reinforce a chosen token with a lime fill.
Do end every choice in a run in the turn block or a rail, with a sentence saying what will happen and one cobalt table button.
Do keep the run route free of app chrome: the corner buttons are its only navigation.
Do keep what names a hand card (sprite, points, cost, name, Info) in its left strip, and tilt only a card at rest; anything being read stands upright.
Do make actions on the table from `TableButton`: cobalt for the one confirm, cream for the rest.
Do set the pixel face at 20px or 30px, or at 40px for a heading on the landing page, and only for print on the board.
Do give every key a visible hint on its piece, shown only for a fine pointer, and keep every keyed action reachable by tap.
Do keep page copy and controls at 48px touch height or more; nothing interactive in play goes below 40px unless its hit area is extended.
Do write counts and scores in tabular figures and labels in sentence case.
Do give every loading surface a skeleton in the shape of its content, and every error a plain sentence and a retry.

Do build the landing page from the tabletop's own pieces (cat cards, dice, food tokens, the mat, tray wells, nameplates, table buttons) inside its own `.tabletop` scope, with no app shell around them.
Do keep a crowd cat decorative: a whole multiple of 16, no label, no clicks, a flat cast only where it stands on the ground.
donts: Don't round the corners of a game piece.
Don't give a piece a blurred shadow, a diagonal offset shadow, or a glow. Outside the tabletop a piece has no shadow at all; inside it has only the straight-down edge and cast.
Don't bring the cardboard edge, the cloth, or the pixel face to home, the codex, auth, or a dialog.
Don't put a 2px ink border or square corners on page chrome, and don't lay a white rounded panel or a pill button on the tabletop.
Don't draw a ring outside a piece's border to show state.
Don't use coral for a decision the player owes or for a card the player is trimming; coral is the rival's.
Don't set the pixel face at any size but 20px and 30px, or 40px for a landing heading, or use it for rules text.
Don't set readable text below 10px, or below 11px on a piece from 640px up.
Don't ease tabletop motion smoothly or fade pieces in; lifts, presses, flips, and rolls move in steps.
Don't use gradients or emoji anywhere.
Don't use raster or smoothed creature art; a cat is its 16x16 sprite.
Don't use an element hue for a panel, a button, or a heading.
Don't use lime for anything the rival owns, or coral for a reward. The landing ribbon is the only lime that is not the player's.
Don't introduce currency, shop, or premium styling; nothing is for sale.
